ticket: PL-11 — A proportionate lite lane for genuinely small tickets
goal: Give routine, very-small work a sanctioned, proportionate path through the pipeline — a /pipeline-lite lane that runs planner -> dev -> tester -> review -> ledger, deliberately skipping red and security, gated by mechanically-checkable smallness/sensitivity bounds and recorded in the ledger as a visibly-distinct lite entry that names exactly which stages were skipped. Today the only alternatives for a one-file maintenance fix are the full six-stage run (disproportionate), /hotfix (requires a production incident), or an unrecorded hand-edit — the D-005 #3 failure the pipeline exists to prevent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: .sdd/pipeline.md contains a `### /pipeline-lite <ticket>` section defining the lane runtime-neutrally: the fail-closed eligibility gate first, the exact stages run (planner -> dev -> tester -> review -> ledger), the two stages deliberately skipped (red, security), reuse of the existing routing and 3-attempt loop cap, the mandatory ledger step, and the disambiguation from /hotfix and /re-gate. The command also appears in that file's intro paragraph and its Entry points preamble list.

The lite lane introduces no new subagent stage: the surviving review-shaped gate is `review` itself, unchanged, and .sdd/pipeline.md's new section says so explicitly, naming scripts/guard-checker-readonly.mjs's READ_ONLY_AGENTS set as where that stage's read-only property is structurally enforced. .sdd/runtimes.yml and every file under .claude/agents/ are unchanged by this ticket.

The surviving verdict gate keeps the JSON-sidecar contract unchanged: the decision is read from .pipeline/review.json through scripts/pipeline-contracts.mjs's strict reader, its `stamp` comes from scripts/write-stamp.mjs, and --lite refuses on a STALE review.json via the existing refuseIfStale. No markdown file is parsed for any lite control decision anywhere in this ticket.

(Amended in this ticket's security-fix round.) .sdd/bounds.yml carries a `lite_eligibility:` block with max_files, max_changed_lines, and max_line_length, and .sdd/bounds.md carries a matching human-facing section that disambiguates `lanes:` (a path fence) from the lite lane (which stages run), and states that lite's barred-path set is the computed union of hotfix_barred_paths and deny_for_fenced_lanes — no third list. hotfix_barred_paths itself (one of the two lists the union draws from, not a new list) was widened in the same fix round — the 'no third list' constraint governs the union mechanism, not either list's contents.

(Amended in this ticket's security-fix round.) readBounds() in scripts/check-bounds.mjs additionally returns liteEligibility: { maxFiles, maxChangedLines, maxLineLength } | null (maxLineLength added by the fix round), returning null (never exiting) when the block is absent or any one of the three keys is missing/malformed. Every existing return key, every existing caller (main(), and ledger-append.mjs's --hotfix path), and check-bounds.mjs's CLI behavior are unchanged.

(Amended in this ticket's security-fix round.) scripts/check-lite-eligible.mjs exists and computes the eligibility verdict mechanically, exiting 0 (eligible) / 1 (ineligible) / 2 (could not run), supporting --files, --base, and --json, and refusing an unrecognized argument by name. It imports readBounds and matchesAny from scripts/check-bounds.mjs rather than re-implementing glob matching or the bounds read, and exports evaluateLiteEligibility / countChangedLines / resolveWorktreeFiles / liteBarredPaths / maxChangedLineLength (the last one added by the fix round) for in-process reuse.

node scripts/ledger-append.mjs --lite writes a lite ledger entry only after every one of these holds, checked in order, refusing with exit 1 and writing nothing (not even a partial run directory) on the first failure: --lite is not combined with --override-security or --re-gate; review.json exists, is not STALE, and reads PASS (or is accepted via --override-review "<reason>"); no FRESH-stamped security.json exists; spec.md/spec.json exist, agree on the ticket, and spec.json carries a stamp; .pipeline/test-results.md exists; the live touched-file set is eligible under evaluateLiteEligibility; and .sdd/ledger/<runId>/ does not already exist.

A lite run's entry.json carries lite: { skippedStages: ["red","security"], note, eligibility: { fileCount, changedLines, maxFiles, maxChangedLines } } with skippedStages and note derived by the script and never caller-supplied; verdicts: { review: "PASS", security: "SKIPPED_LITE" }; securityRunId: null; redTestPaths: [] with a lite-specific redAbsenceNote; regate: null; overrides: []; and bypass: false.

A lite run's entry.md is headed `# Ledger entry — <runId> (LITE)` and carries a `## Lite lane` section, placed immediately after `## Verdicts`, naming the skipped stages, the fixed disclosure note (what was therefore not verified), and the eligibility numbers this run was measured against.

buildEntryJson's bypass derivation is amended to reviewVerdict !== 'PASS' || (!lite && securityVerdict !== 'PASS'), so an ordinary lite entry is bypass: false (and therefore indexed) while --lite --override-review still produces bypass: true (and therefore excluded), exactly like any other overridden entry.

scripts/build-ledger-index.mjs indexes a lite entry rather than excluding it, and carries lite: { skippedStages } into every index.json record that run produces. Its verdicts gate accepts { review: "PASS", security: "SKIPPED_LITE" } only when the entry declares a lite object whose skippedStages includes "security", and continues to enforce byte-for-byte { review: "PASS", security: "PASS" } on every other non-bypass entry.

.sdd/ledger/README.md carries a "Lite-lane entries" section documenting the exact lite/verdicts shape, the decision to index a lite entry (with its reason, and the contrast against a --hotfix/override entry's exclusion), and what a lite entry structurally lacks: no security/ copy, no security.json, no red.json.

.claude/skills/pipeline-lite/SKILL.md exists, is thin and consistent with the other shims (frontmatter name, description, disable-model-invocation: true, argument-hint; body pointing at .sdd/pipeline.md's section without restating its procedure), and scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs gains a generalized assertion that every `### /<command>` section in .sdd/pipeline.md has a matching .claude/skills/<command>/SKILL.md.

Wiring exists and is gated: package.json declares check:lite-eligible and test:lite-eligible; .github/workflows/ci.yml runs npm run test:lite-eligible; scripts/tsconfig.json's include lists both new files. scripts/sdd-completeness.test.mjs's two existing generalized assertions (every scripts/*.test.mjs has a test:* script and a CI step; every check:<suffix> has a test:<suffix> naming a real file) must pass without being weakened.

Test coverage exists for every script touched: a new scripts/check-lite-eligible.test.mjs, plus [lite]-tagged cases added to scripts/ledger-append.test.mjs, scripts/build-ledger-index.test.mjs, and scripts/check-bounds.test.mjs. No existing assertion in any of those suites is weakened or removed to accommodate this change.

.sdd/stages/tester.md is amended so red.md's absence is a legitimate state on the lite lane (state it, do not stop), while its D-018 guarantee is preserved in force: tester still never authors a behavioral test and still reports gaps rather than filling them. The Output contract's "Red suite result" bullet requires an explicit statement when no red suite exists. .sdd/stages/CHANGELOG.md records the round. No other stage file's procedure is changed.

.sdd/pipeline.md's new section carries an "Honest limits" paragraph naming exactly what this lane gives up: red's spec-first ordering (any test for this ticket is written after the diff exists — the D-018 inversion, reintroduced deliberately and only here), security's full attacker-brief sweep, the CORE-01..06 mandatory checks, and the immutable .pipeline/security-history/ audit record; that the barred-path list is curated and best-effort rather than a complete classifier; and the fail-closed default that ambiguous eligibility routes to /pipeline.

The lane is discoverable from where a person actually looks: .sdd/hotfix.md's "When this is the right call" section routes "a fix that is too small to need a spec" to /pipeline-lite instead of leaving that list with no alternative; CLAUDE.md's Agent pipeline related-commands list and .sdd/README.md's directory map and skills paragraph both name it.

edgeCases.text: Eligibility is ambiguous or unknown at entry (the paths cannot be named confidently, or check-lite-eligible.mjs exits 2): route to /pipeline. Ambiguity is ineligibility; the lane is never entered provisionally. The same routing table covers the two adjacent cases: a small change during a production incident is /hotfix, and a small change on a barred path is /pipeline.

(Amended in this ticket's security-fix round.) The realized diff exceeds max_files, max_changed_lines, or (added by the fix round — see EC-21) max_line_length at ledger time: --lite refuses (exit 1), naming the actual counts, the bounds they exceeded, and the sanctioned escalation (run /security, then the plain node scripts/ledger-append.mjs). No ledger entry and no partial run directory are written.

(Amended in this ticket's security-fix round.) The realized diff touches a path in the barred union: --lite refuses, naming every matching path and which list it came from. hotfix_barred_paths was widened by the fix round to also cover services/core/src/services/**, services/core/src/routes/**, services/core/src/mcp/**, services/workers/**, and services/gateway/**.
A binary (or otherwise unsizable) file appears in the diff — git diff --numstat reports -/- for it: the change is ineligible. A change that cannot be measured is never measured as small.

.pipeline/review.json's stamp is STALE: --lite refuses via the existing refuseIfStale, unchanged from the plain path, and still refuses when --override-review is supplied (an override accepts a real non-PASS verdict, never one computed against a tree that has since moved on).

.pipeline/review.json reads NEEDS_FIXES: --lite refuses unless --override-review "<reason>" is supplied; with it, the entry is written, bypass is true, and the entry is excluded from index.json's file->spec map exactly like any other overridden entry.
--lite --override-security: refused, naming why — there is no security verdict on this lane to override, and accepting the flag silently would imply one existed.

--lite --re-gate: refused in this ticket, naming the route (finish through the full lane — run /security, then --re-gate — or re-run /review against the current tree and use plain --lite, which the non-stale review.json requirement already forces).

A .pipeline/security.json exists whose stamp reads FRESH: --lite refuses and points at the plain node scripts/ledger-append.mjs. A security run that genuinely happened against this tree must never be recorded as SKIPPED_LITE.

A .pipeline/security.json exists whose stamp reads STALE or unknown (a leftover from a prior ticket): it is ignored for this run's verdict, with an explicit printed note saying so, and is never copied into the lite entry.

A .pipeline/red.json exists (a leftover, or red genuinely ran earlier in this checkout): a lite entry never copies it and never lists its tests as this run's red-test paths. redAbsenceNote states that red was deliberately skipped by the lite lane — not the existing "predates the red stage" wording, which would be a different and false claim.
.pipeline/test-results.md is missing: --lite refuses, saying tester still runs on this lane and naming which stage must run first.

.pipeline/spec.json carries no stamp: --lite refuses, the same hygiene check --re-gate already applies, and for a stated reason — --lite has no security-history cross-check to compensate. As with --re-gate, this is presence-and-shape, never proof of provenance.

.pipeline/spec.json's ticket disagrees with .pipeline/spec.md's first-heading ticket: the existing unconditional agreement check refuses, on the --lite path exactly as on every other. Pinned as a regression so the new branch cannot accidentally bypass a check that is currently unconditional.

An entry.json claims verdicts.security: "SKIPPED_LITE" with no lite object, or with a lite.skippedStages that omits "security": build-ledger-index.mjs refuses to index the run and --check fails loudly. A non-lite entry can never launder a skipped gate into an indexed one.

.sdd/bounds.yml's lite_eligibility block is absent or malformed: readBounds().liteEligibility is null, check-lite-eligible.mjs exits 2, and ledger-append.mjs --lite refuses. A missing bound is never read as "no bound," and --hotfix's own use of readBounds() is unaffected.

The working tree is already clean (the fix is committed) and there is no changes.json: filesTouched's existing loud failure applies unchanged, and — where it does return a list — eligibility is still evaluated against it; if nothing can be sized, the check reports "could not run" and --lite refuses rather than recording an unmeasured change as small.
.sdd/ledger/<runId>/ already exists: refuse rather than overwrite, the same guard main() already applies, reached on the lite path too.

A previous run's ledger output (.sdd/ledger/<prior-run>/..., .sdd/ledger/index.json) is still uncommitted in the working tree when the next lite run reaches its ledger step: those paths are under .sdd/**, which is in the barred union, so the run is refused, with a message saying to commit the previous ledger entry first. Recorded as a known, accepted cost rather than carved out — a carve-out for .sdd/ledger/** would also permit a lite ticket to rewrite committed ledger history with no security pass.

A lite run and a full run both touch the same file: index.json[<file>] holds both records, and the lite one carries lite: { skippedStages } so a reader following the fast path (buggy file -> index.json) sees the attribution is qualified without a second hop into entry.json — the same reasoning regate: { testerRan } already uses.

(Added in this ticket's security-fix round — security round FND-22ef4b5c746e, MEDIUM.) The realized diff is shaped as a very few, very long lines such that changedLines stays comfortably under max_changed_lines while the diff carries real, substantial content: max_line_length is the orthogonal bound evaluateLiteEligibility/maxChangedLineLength check independently of line count, and --lite refuses (exit 1) on it exactly like any other eligibility violation, naming the measured length and the bound it exceeded. Enforced fail-closed the same way as the other two bounds (EC-16): a lite_eligibility block missing max_line_length reads as null, never as "no bound."
